sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The maamar questions why the verse says "parzono" instead of "pizrono," and explains that the scattering of Israel among the nations is meant to elevate them to the level of "parzones" (openness) of Jerusalem.

translations.translation: And the maamar22 points out,
that according to this interpretation of "tzedek parzono"
(charity etc. that He scattered them etc.)
it should have said "tzedek pizrono" — why does it say "parzono"?
And he explains23,
that "parzono" is like the verse24
"Parzot teishev Yerushalayim" (Jerusalem shall dwell as open villages).
That is,

the charity that the Holy One, blessed be He, did with Israel in scattering them among the nations is in order that through this they will reach a higher level than they were before the descent of their scattering,
even to the level of "parzot teishev Yerushalayim"
(parzono).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This is understood through the concept that everything in the world exists in man, and thus the spiritual aspect of Jerusalem — complete awe — is eternal in every Jew even during exile.

translations.translation: And this will be understood based on the Sages' statement25
that everything that exists in the world exists in man
[therefore man is called a small world26,
and each person is obligated to say "for my sake the world was created"27].
From this it is understood,
that in man,
"you are called man"28,
there is the aspect of Jerusalem.
That is,
that even during the time of exile, when "because of our sins we were exiled from our land and distanced from our soil"29
[this matter
(we were exiled from our land and distanced from our soil)
applies also to the children of Israel who are in the Holy Land, may it be built and established30],
nevertheless,
the spiritual concept of Jerusalem is eternal even now,
in each and every Jew.
And the explanation is,
that it is known31
that Yerushalayim means "yirah shalem" (complete awe)
[and this matter applies also regarding the actual city of Jerusalem,
as it is brought in Tosafot32
in the name of the Midrash33
that the name Yerushalayim is from "Shalem" which Malki Tzedek king of Shalem called it, and from "Yirah" which Avraham called it],
which is the completeness of awe.
And this is that the spiritual Jerusalem is eternal even now during the time of exile,
for in each and every Jew, even during the time of exile, there is
(at least in a concealed state)
the completeness of awe,
as will be explained below.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: There are two interpretations of Jerusalem (complete awe) in divine service: the revealed levels of lower and higher awe, and the essential point of awe that transcends revelation and is always present in every Jew.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by first prefacing,
that regarding the concept of Jerusalem
(completeness of awe)
in man's divine service,
there are two interpretations.
For in many places34
it is explained that Jerusalem is the awe as it comes in the form of awe,
and this is the concept of the lower Jerusalem and the upper Jerusalem,
for in awe there are generally two levels,
lower awe — the lower Jerusalem,
and higher awe — the upper Jerusalem.
And this is the statement of the Holy One, blessed be He, "I will not enter the upper Jerusalem until I enter the lower Jerusalem"35,
for although in terms of revelations, lower awe is very low compared to higher awe,
nevertheless,
since lower awe has its root in higher awe36,
to the extent that both are one37,
therefore,
through lower awe
(the lower Jerusalem)
one reaches higher awe
(the upper Jerusalem)38.
And from the continuation of the topics in this maamar it is understood39,
that Jerusalem is the point of fear of Heaven that is above intellect,
a point that is above form,
which exists in each and every Jew,
from the essence of the soul within him that is above revelations40.
And it can be said,
that among the reasons why this point is called by the name Jerusalem,
completeness of awe,
is,
that the true meaning of completeness is that it cannot have any deficiency.
Therefore,
awe as it comes in revelation
(in the form of awe),
since it is possible for it to have a deficiency,
does not have true completeness,
and true completeness is in the point of fear of Heaven that is above revelation,
for this point always exists in each and every Jew.
